reason: Every load-bearing claim survives driving. lately.html:851 interpolates `${j.title}, ${j.age} days` for every job — the one age string on this surface that does not go through plural() (line 678), while its siblings at 835 (the mark's aria-label and its data-tip) and 843 (the Oldest label) all do. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 in both grounds across all seven states, reading .card.ages p.sr: quiet speaks 'Order tonic and the good olives, 1 days'; first-run speaks it three times, verbatim as the seat quotes it ('Confirm the Harbour wall cordon with the harbourmaster, 1 days; Order tonic and the good olives, 1 days; Send the midweek rate to the June 2027 couple, 1 days'). The fixture confirms why: scopes.quiet ages are [1,2,3,4,6,7,9,11,12] and scopes.first-run are [1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3], while full and partial start at 2 — so the full state hides it by fixture accident, exactly as claimed. The p.sr has no aria-hidden ancestor and computes display:block, so it is live in the tree, and one tab-press away the same mark's accessible name reads 'open 1 day' — the same fact spoken two ways inside one card. Not already handled: round 1's count-of-one-takes-a-plural-verb landed on the KPI row's verb concord (see the source comment at 718-722); this noun never entered that fix. Not a gate restatement — the opposite, and this is the more valuable half. interaction-check.mjs carries a grammar gate, 'every sentence agrees with its own numeral', that drives full/partial/quiet/first-run and scans `main p, main span, .sr` — the exact nodes carrying this string — but its three regexes test only verb concord (jobs has/is/was, 1 job have/are/were, All 1 open job). It has no noun-concord test, so it reads '1 days' in two of the four states it drives and passes green. I swept all seven states for a singular numeral followed by a plural noun, across textContent, aria-label and data-tip: quiet and first-run return ['1 days'] and the other five return nothing, so the seat's 'it is the last one left' is measured true rather than rhetorical. Severity holds at defect: the numeral is correct and the sentence asserts nothing untrue, so it is not misleading; nothing fails to work, so it is not blocking. It is plainly wrong copy in the one channel where this surface is nothing but its copy. Confirmed as filed.
sharpenedFix: The seat's fix is exact and correct — in lately.html:851 replace `${j.title}, ${j.age} days` with `${j.title}, ${plural(j.age, "day", "days")}`; plural(1,'day','days') yields '1 day' and plural(2,...) yields '2 days', so full and partial come out byte-identical. The target string occurs exactly once in the file. Take the gate hole with it, which is worth more than the defect: inside the check() of the 'every sentence agrees with its own numeral' block in interaction-check.mjs, add a noun-concord test for a bare '1' followed by days/jobs/weeks/hours, and watch it fail on quiet and first-run BEFORE applying the line-851 change, so the new assertion is proven non-vacuous rather than added already-green.
breaks: Nothing. No gate assertion reads this string's day-count: interaction-check.mjs:807 and :852 parse 'open (N) days?' off dot aria-labels (untouched by this fix), :813 parses '(N) job has|jobs have been open longer' from this same p.sr but matches only its trailing clause, and :158 asserts only that each .sr carries real text. The audit gate does not read copy. Re-measure after it lands: run interaction-check.mjs in full (461 assertions) and re-drive ?state=quiet and ?state=first-run at 1440 in both grounds to confirm the sr line reads '..., 1 day; ...' and that full and partial are unchanged. One adjacent observation, deliberately outside this fix's scope: j.title is interpolated raw on 851 where the dot at 835 uses esc(j.title). Titles come from the build-checked fixture so nothing is exploitable today, and widening this finding to cover it would be scope creep — but if the line is being touched anyway, esc() is the consistent call.
